ares_pc.releaseNotes:
ares v148 has now been released.

This release includes big improvements to a number of ares cores. Highlights include rewrites to the N64 CPU & RSP JITs resulting in significant performance gains across the N64 library, additional implementation & accuracy improvements to the PlayStation core, fixes to the GBA core, and support for the Famicom data recorder & Dendy. 

Additionally, there have been many updates to the core ares application across all platforms. Per-core input configuration has been added, updated video, audio, & input drivers are available, bug fixes, additional options have been added, and core dependencies have been updated. 

Since v147, 20 contributors have created 300 commits to the ares codebase.

As always, if you wish to see the full changelog in a per-commit format along with their authors, you can do so on GitHub [here](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/compare/v147...v148).

**NOTE**: The signing certificate used to sign ares on Windows has expired. ares will be unsigned until a compatible signing solution is found. Windows users should be sure to only download ares from official sources, including the ares [website](https://ares-emu.net/download) and [GitHub](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/releases/tag/v148).


**Sony - PlayStation**

 - Refactored core to use libco threading
 - CPU: implemented memory timing/control registers
 - CD-ROM: incorrect 150 LBA offset in command 0x14
 - CD-ROM: fix behavior when a command is issued before the previous has completed
 - CD-ROM: implement behavior where a new command cannot be executed until pending       
 - CD-ROM: implement 'command/parameter busy' register
 - DMA: improve chopping/allowing the cpu to run between blocks of a long transfer
 - DMA: fixed incorrect bit position for DMA channel chopping enable
 - DMA: fixed block DMA using incorrect timing
 - DMA: fixed SPU canReadDMA/canWriteDMA flags
 - MDEC: implement basic decode timing
 - MDEC: implement correct input fifo behavior
 - MDEC: fix behavior when an incomplete block is transferred via the input fifo
 - MDEC: fix DMA request registers, input/output full/empty registers, busy register
 - GPU: use correct clock frequency for PAL and NTSC
 - GPU: fix hblank timing
 - GPU: Fixed some clocking issues
 - Timer: improve behavior around timer overflow/target reached IRQ

**Nintendo - Game Boy Advance**

 - Only trigger keypad IRQ when input changes
 - Fixed handling of repeat bit during immediate DMA transfers
 - Prefetcher should fail reading across 128KiB boundaries
 - OBJ mosaic fixes to correct some graphical bugs
 - Prevent instruction tracing from modifying open bus
 - Refactored bus reads fixing some open bus edge cases
 - Implemented internal horizontal/vertical window flags when window boundaries reached
 - Improved affine parameter timings
 - Fixed wave RAM bank selection
 - Added OAM to memory viewer
 - Implemented OAM stage timings for sprite rendering

**Nintendo - Super Famicom / SNES**

 - Added support for loading GBC games in the Super Game Boy
 - Super Game Boy accuracy fixes (multiplayer, packet acknowledgement, register mirroring)
 - Improved auto-joypad polling accuracy

**Nintendo - Nintendo 64**

 - CPU & RSP JIT improvements resulting in improved performance 
 - Cubivore (Doubutsu Banchou w/English patch applied) support added
 - Implemented support for region free ROMs (homebrew extension)
 - If homebrew header present, don’t default to a controller pak in port 1
 - Keep serrate bit enabled when VI processing is disabled
 - Fixed audio pops when AI DMA ends
 - Fixed GDB read result for RCP/PI bus path
 - Implemented eeprom write timing and status flags
 - Added initial support for Emux extensions
 - Implemented VR4300 reverse-endian mode

**Nintendo - Famicom / NES**

 - Added support for the Famicom data recorder
 - Added support for JY Company and SC-127 boards
 - Added support for the Dendy…

armsx2.releaseNotes:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- Android: ARMSX2_BUILD_EERUNNER requires ENABLE_RECOMPILER_TEST_HOOKS
- Android: add the USE_PERF_JITDUMP build option
- Android: make pcsx2-eerunner buildable as an NDK executable
- Android: regenerate the PGO profile on the Adreno 722 source
- Android PGO: record internal-linkage functions by file name, not build path
- GS: trim one native pixel off each edge when upscaling 2x or more
- GameDB: nativeCounterDraws for Shadow of the Colossus
- GS: nativeCounterDraws, draw colour-wrap counter draws at native resolution
- GameDB: OPHFlagHack for Shadow of the Colossus, as NetherSX2 has it

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/nightly-20261022...90126bdfea7a3ffb1fd288b2f7f0ae0b033af2d6

armsx3.releaseNotes: # ARMSX3 1.3.2 ## Online - **RPCN has been updated so sign-in works again with the latest RPCN server**, including its new title storage (TSS) support that some games use online. ## Controls - **New option: Tight L1/L2/R1/R2 touch areas**, in Settings > Controls > On-Screen Controls. The shoulder buttons respond only on the button itself, and their outlines in the touch layout editor fit the buttons. (In the next ARMSX2 nightly as well). ## Home screen - **Home screen shortcuts show the game's cover** instead of the ARMSX3 icon. (In the next ARMSX2 nightly as well). (P.S. The Yakuza Dead Souls fix is already in ARMSX3! Start Yakuza and open All Core Settings from the in-game menu, so the setting only applies to that game. Search “PPU Event” and the setting PPU Event Wake-Up Delay will appear. Set PPU Event Wake-Up Delay (between 0 and 200 µs, experiment with what works for your device). The 60 FPS patch: FlexBy’s patch is in RPCS3’s patch database for BLUS30826, BLES01399 and NPEB02034. Tap Download / update patch database in the Patches tab and it shows up for the game. Once your done close the game and reopen it.

azahar_plus.releaseNotes:
⚠️⚠️⚠️
This version fixes a critical security vulnerability that was publicly announced so immediate update is advised
https://github.com/azahar-emu/azahar/security/advisories/GHSA-h74v-5mw8-qg8r
⚠️⚠️⚠️

AzaharPlus 2126.2-A is the same as Azahar 2126.2 except for this:

- Compatibility with all game files. If a file works with any Citra fork, it works with AzaharPlus.
- Ability to download system files from official servers. No need for an actual 3DS.
- Compatibility with older CPUs (no SSE4.2 required)
- Compatibility with Android 9
- ZipPass: A new way to exchange StreetPass data through zip files
- Built in cheats
- Amiibo generation

copperline_pc.releaseNotes:
Copperline 1.0.1 is the first maintenance release for 1.0. Most of it fixes problems reported against 1.0.0: an AGA display fetch error, a blitter race on fast CPUs, warm reboots on the A3000 and A4000, the 68060 FPU at reset, the copperhf hard-disk driver, and a window-resize hang on Windows. Menu settings are now remembered between launches, and screenshots save the picture as you see it.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.1.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files still load: the save-state format has not changed, and a 1.0.0 state resumes byte-for-byte as it does in 1.0.0.
- **Settings changed from the menu are now saved.** In 1.0.0 they lasted for the session. Now a change made from the menu, a hotkey or the status bar is written into your saved default configuration, which is created if you do not have one. Sessions started with `--config`, a `./copperline.toml` or `--factory` leave their files alone, and scheduled headless runs never write. See [settings the menu remembers](https://copperline.dev/docs/ui/#settings-the-menu-remembers).
- **The screenshot shortcuts have changed.** `Cmd+S` / `Alt+S` and the status-bar camera now save the picture as it is displayed (see below). Native 1:1 screenshots have their own shortcut, `Cmd+Option+S` on macOS and `Ctrl+Alt+S` on Linux and Windows. The **Video Settings -> Native Screenshot Button** item is gone. `[recording] native_screenshot_button` is still accepted, so configurations load, but it is ignored. `--native-screenshots` still selects native captures for `--screenshot-after` and `--expect-screenshot`.
- **Native screenshots of interlaced screens are now full height.** A 640x512 laced screen saves at 640x512, not 640x256. Expectation images made with `--native-screenshots` on an interlaced screen need re-capturing.
- **`--mouse-to-after` and `--pen-after` coordinates now match `--screenshot-after` pixels**, as the documentation always said. 1.0.0 used the coordinates of the unframed field, so scripts tuned to that may need new targets. The control protocol's `input.mouse_to` and `input.pen` keep their `capture.screenshot` coordinates.
- **The 68060 starts with its FPU disabled**, as on real 68060 boards, and `68060.library` turns it on. Without that library a 68060 system runs with no FPU, even with `fpu = true`.
- **Going back to 1.0.0:** 1.0.0 refuses configuration files that use the new `[display] track_display` or `[audio] floppy_sounds_set` keys.

## AGA bitplane fetch stop

AGA's Alice keeps the hardwired `$D8` bitplane fetch stop, just as ECS Agnus does. The stop is lifted only while BEAMCON0 selects HARDDIS or VARBEAMEN, or BPLCON0 selects super-hires or ultra-hires. Copperline treated every AGA machine as if HARDDIS were set and let the fetch run to `$E0`. A program that sets DDFSTOP past `$D8` then fetched an extra word on every line, and its picture slanted further down the screen. Pacmania under WHDLoad on an A1200 is one example. A new test program checks the stop and each control that lifts it.

## Blitter on 68020 and faster CPUs

BBUSY drops with the last cycle of a blit, two colour clocks before the final word is written. A 68020 or faster CPU polling DMACONR can start setting up the next blit inside that gap. Copperline let a BLTCON0 write there cancel the pending write, so the final word was lost, and for a one-word, one-line blit the whole result. The end-of-blit register write-back could also overwrite registers already set for the next blit. Now BLTCON0 cancels the pending write only while BBUSY is set, and the registers are written back once, when BBUSY drops. A 68000 is too slow to hit the gap. This fixes bitplanes missing from small `graphics.library` copies on an A4000 with Kickstart 3.2 (#573). Thanks to @codewiz for the report.

You need to map the analog triggers to DS buttons or special function keys first.
If your controller does not have analog triggers, or if its L2/R2 buttons generate both button events and analog trigger events at the same time (which may cause mapped buttons to be triggered twice), it is recommended to disable this option.

### 🎮 Right Analog Stick Mode
Added a new `D-Pad` mode for the right analog stick, allowing it to be used for directional input.
And `D-Pad` mode is now the default mode for the right analog stick. You can still disable the right analog stick in the settings if desired.

Decide the rotation mode of the left and right analog sticks on the controller.
Supporting 'Turn Left', 'Turn Right', and 'Rotate 180°'.

### New option: Display the DS Bottom Screen in Single-Screen Layouts
A new option allows the DS bottom screen to be shown by default when using single-screen layouts.
If your dual-screen handheld gaming device has the bottom screen as the main screen, it is highly recommended to enable this option for a better screen-swap experience.

gse_speedrun.releaseNotes:
Sixth release of GSE.

This release replaces the GBA emulation core. Previously, [mGBA's](https://github.com/mgba-emu/mgba) GBA emulation core was used for GBA games. GSE now uses [Mesen's](https://github.com/nesdev-org/MesenCE) GBA emulation core for GBA games. This offers far better accuracy, to the point even GBA Pokémon TASes can sync on console, and as such emulator players can fairly compete with console players in GBA Pokémon speedrunners, along with likely many other games.

This release also features various bugfixes, along with minor QoL improvements such as an option to automatically hide the mouse cursor, saving the last used emulator width/height for when no ROM is loaded (i.e. no longer hardcoding GBA resolution), and more.

This release will likely be the last release for various old platforms (for macOS < 12, Linux < glibc 2.35, and Android < 7), mainly due to dependencies dropping support. This shouldn't affect most users, but it is noted for whatever users still use these old platforms.

Several download options are available, for various OSes and CPU architectures, per the [requirements listed in the README](https://github.com/CasualPokePlayer/GSE/blob/v0.6/README.md#user-requirements). For most users (with a Windows machine on an x64 device), the `GSE-win-x64.zip` file should be downloaded.

kytyplus_pc.releaseNotes:
# KytyPlus v5.0

One fix, and it is a compatibility one: PS5 packages no longer abort during installation on
titles whose filesystem metadata is not the last thing in the package.

## Package installation (issue #20)

- **Gran Turismo 7's package failed before listing a single file.** The installer reported
  `Invalid package range: offset=25FC1FD8031, length=3FFDC, total=1F27EE0000` — a read 2.6 TB past
  the end of a 134 GB package. The offset was never the problem; the position it came from was.
- **How the position is chosen was the bug.** The package layout lists one boundary per file, and
  the installer took the highest boundary that was 64 KiB-aligned and treated it as the start of the
  game's filesystem. That granularity is finer than the mount is served in: blocks are 256 KiB, so
  a boundary 128 KiB inside a block is a file tail, not a superblock. Decoding a file tail is what
  produced the impossible offset.
- **The position is now proven by decoding it, not guessed.** Candidates are required to sit on a
  real block boundary and are tried from the top down until one yields an actual PS5 filesystem
  superblock, which is the position every later read depends on. Up to 512 candidates are tried;
  each is a single block decode, so a package that resolves on the first candidate costs what it
  used to.
- **Failures now say which record broke.** A block address that lands outside the package reports
  the records that produced it — the run record, its raw bits, the gap and the accumulated offset —
  instead of a bare range check that cannot be compared between two packages. Running the extractor
  with `KYTY_NAPS_TRACE=1` additionally reports the outer filesystem's flags, including whether a
  package is encrypted, and the layout header's table sizes.

## Known issues

- **This is verified not to regress the one PS5 package we can test here** — it resolves at the same
  position on the first candidate and extracts every file — but Gran Turismo 7 itself has not been
  installed by us, and we will not ask anyone to send a dump. If a package's compressed-block
  addressing also breaks at that size, installation will now fail later, with a message that names
  the records, so the next report is actionable rather than a dead end.
- **Encrypted PS5 packages still cannot be installed.** That is unchanged and not fixable here:
  retail package keys are not available, so only packages that carry the plain or debug marker get
  past the outer filesystem.
- PS4 packages and `.ffpfsc` images do not use this code path at all, so neither is affected either
  way.

mame4droid.releaseNotes:
#  Rollback NetPlay: compatibility and stability

Rollback is what makes NetPlay feel like two people on one machine instead of
two people waiting for each other. This release is mostly about the games that
could not use it, and the sessions that fell apart halfway through.

## Street Fighter III now runs in rollback

All of CPS-3 does: 3rd Strike and the earlier two, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure,
Red Earth. Until now these were stuck in Lockstep, which is the worst place for
a fighting game to be.

The problem was size. To rewind, rollback keeps dozens of snapshots of the
machine in memory, and a CPS-3 snapshot was enormous — it carried the entire
game loaded from the CD, tens of megabytes of code, graphics and samples that
never change while you play. Snapshots now leave all of that behind and keep
only what the game actually writes to. What used to be far past any sane limit
now fits with room to spare.

Games that already fit benefit too: smaller snapshots mean less memory and less
work on every correction.

## More games run in rollback

The host now hands its machine state to the joiner by default, so games that
used to refuse rollback because both sides could not be trusted to boot
identically now qualify.

## Sessions that used to break

**Joining and resyncing.** A drop-in join or a mid-game resync would sometimes
leave one machine frozen, or the joiner on a black screen, with nothing to do
but disconnect. The snapshot was being taken wherever the emulation happened to
be at that instant, sometimes in the middle of a frame with work still pending.
It is now always taken at the end of a frame, once the video chip has finished
and the interrupt queue is drained. The state that arrives is one the other
machine can actually resume from.

**Brief network drops.** Lose enough packets in a row and one frame would stay
a guess forever: the game kept running, quietly wrong, and the two sides drifted
apart over the next minutes. That frame is now re-requested from the other
player and the session repairs itself. Tested by cutting the connection on
purpose, over and over.

**Dials, spinners and 4-way sticks.** Part of the live control state was not
included in a rollback, so analog games could jump or fall back to a stale
reading after a correction. It travels with the state now.

## Quick messages

The last release said there would be no chat, and there still isn't one. What
there is now is a short list of fixed phrases — hello, good game, wait a moment,
insert coin and press start, I have to go. Picking one sends a number, not text,
and the other player's device shows that phrase in their own language. Nothing
typed, nothing to moderate, nothing stored. You can mute the ones you receive.

## Drop-in BIOS selection

For games with several BIOS versions, the picker was starting on an arbitrary
one and, if you pressed Exit instead of choosing, it published your room anyway.
It now starts on the game's default BIOS, and Exit cancels the whole thing.

## Smaller things

- Dialogs start with a sensible button selected, so a gamepad can go through
  NetPlay without touching the screen. Disconnect is never the one selected,
  and it now sits at the bottom of the menu, away from the rest.
- The public room board shows the busiest countries on a line of its own.

## Both devices must be updated

The network protocol changed. An updated device and an old one will refuse each
other when connecting, which is deliberate: the alternative is a session that
looks fine and slowly falls apart.

# NgpCraft Emulator v3.12 - what's new

New features, netplay fix attempt. **If you play mirror matches online,
both players must update**: this version cannot play a mirror match with 3.9.1 or older.

## New features

- **Updates from inside the emulator.** *Settings ▸ General ▸ Check for updates* tells you if a
  newer version is out. On Windows and Linux, *Install and restart* downloads it, installs it and
  starts it: no more trip to the GitHub page. On macOS the button opens the download page. The
  emulator also checks by itself at startup, at most once a day, and never interrupts a game
  (untick *Check for updates at startup* if you would rather it did not). Your saves, settings and
  library are kept: only the program file is replaced. **This is the last version you need to
  download by hand.**
- **Run-ahead (optional, off by default).** *Settings ▸ General ▸ Run-ahead*: shows the picture the
  game will draw 1 or 2 frames from now, with the buttons you are holding, so the delay built into
  the game itself disappears from the screen. In *Sonic*, a jump now shows up 4 frames after the
  press instead of 6. It is computed on a separate hidden console: your game, its save, rewind and
  cheats are never affected. It switches itself off during link play, fast-forward and slow motion,
  and pauses for half a second while the game saves.
- **Video recording with sound.** The new ⏺ button next to GIF records an MP4 (640 × 608, sharp
  pixels, music and sound effects) until you click it again, up to ten minutes. Fast-forward and
  slow motion still give a real-speed video. It needs [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) installed;
  without it, the sound is saved as a `.wav`.
- **Fan translations and hacks load by themselves.** Put `Game.ips` or `Game.bps` next to
  `Game.ngc` (for a game inside a `.zip`: next to the zip, named after the game) and the patch is
  applied when the game starts. Your ROM file is never changed, and the game's save goes to the
  separate `.flash` file. A `.bps` made for a different version of the ROM is refused with a clear
  message. Can be turned off in *Settings ▸ General*.
- **RetroArch core: achievements and cheats.** The core now supports RetroAchievements (the Neo Geo
  Pocket sets made for other cores read the same memory) and RetroArch's cheat codes.

- **Hosting an online game no longer fails with `[WinError 10054]` about 20 seconds in.** Since
  3.9.0 the emulator opens its port on your router by itself (UPnP) — and removed that rule as

  Windows machine in the United States, which failed three times before the fix.

  match.** Restarting a console for the match left one of its sound timers in the state the game had
  left it, while the other PC rebuilt that console from scratch: the two copies drifted apart and the
  match ended with "the two consoles no longer match". Found by our new automated link tests, which

# RPCSX-UI app — v2026.07.08-1138

Android frontend. This release adds playing games straight from a folder you pick
(including ISOs), a sortable/filterable library, safer game removal, and RPCN/power UX.

## Game library
- Games folder: scan a folder you choose, in place (all-files access), including
  direct ISO play; boot content:// ISOs via a SAF fd with no extraction
- Sort the library (Last played / Name) and filter it (Installed / Games folder /
  Only played) from persistent top-bar toggles
- De-duplicate the same title across install sources
- Removal reworked: a games-folder entry is never kicked off the list (move its
  file out of the folder to remove it); only installed copies can be deleted, behind
  a confirmation; Clear Cache works for any game (keyed by title id, incl. ISOs); a
  user's source ISO/folder is never deleted
- Storage-permission prompt asked once, up front; robust installed-vs-folder
  classification; onBoot hardened against an unsynced list

## Launch / frontends
- Other frontends (Daijisho, ES-DE, ...) can launch a game directly via intent

## Power / gameplay UX
- Opt-in GPU turbo toggle (max Adreno clocks, off by default), mutually exclusive
  with battery saver, plus an in-game home-menu bridge
- Keep the screen on during long precompiles and gameplay
- Fix quit-to-recents ANR; fix overlay dpad/face-button drift when scaled; show the
  install-failure dialog even when notifications are denied

## Online (RPCN)
- Live connection-status indicator (polled, non-blocking); auto-connect on
  enable/startup; clearer create-vs-sign-in and Test-connection gating

## Stability
- Crash-loop breaker for a core that hard-crashes during load (durable flag);
  ProgressRepository request-id race fix; smooth-shaders toggle in Clanker settings

sameboy_core.releaseNotes:
This version is backwards compatible with save states from SameBoy 0.14.3 and newer, as well as save states from any BESS compliant emulator

## New/Improved Features
* The libretro core now supports API extensions to retrieve additional metadata and create more portable battery save files
* The iOS frontend has been updated with improved iOS 27 support
* iPhone Duo support was added to the iOS frontend
* The CRT scaling filter has been updated with an improved look
* A new Pixelated/Sharp Bilinear scaling filter
    * This new filter is now the default filter in the Cocoa and SDL frontends
* VFS support was added to the libretro core
* Logging support was added to the libretro core
* The libretro core will now render audio directly in the frontend's audio sample rate, if supported
* Recording audio to a VGM log file is now possible in the Cocoa and SDL frontends
* Minor UI improvements in the Cocoa frontend

## Accuracy Improvements/Fixes
* Workboy emulation now correctly reports the current weekday
* Fixed a bug that made certain small ROM files be incorrectly detected as MMM01 cartridges
* More accurate emulation of SGB command processing

## Bug Fixes
* Fixed a bug where periodic battery saves were performed from the wrong thread in the Cocoa frontend, causing debug builds to crash
* Fixed controller hotkeys not working on newer macOS versions in the Cocoa frontend
* Fixed a bug that prevented mapping Load State commands to a controller hotkey in the Cocoa frontend
* The libretro core no longer reports an RTC memory region when emulating cartridges without an RTC
* Fixed a bug that could trigger memory corruptions on x86-64 platforms when loading malformed save states
* Improved sanitization of the Game Boy Printer save state data
* Fixed an incorrectly label “Rumble strength” label in the Cocoa frontend
* File dialogs on Windows now switch Full Screen mode off before they appear, working around bugs in Windows' windowing system
* Fixed a bug that made the Joycon autopair button not work in the Cocoa frontend
* Fixed a bug that made breakpoints created by the `GB_debugger_execute_command` API would not trigger under some conditions when using SameBoy as a library

## Misc Internal Changes
* The build system no longer prints ignored errors when building SameBoy without RGBDS installed if prebuilt boot ROMs are used
* `ibtool` no longer silently fails when building the Cocoa or iOS frontends
* The logging API now has attribute flags that mark if a log line is an error or a warning caused by the previous API call

*2026-10-20*
---

## RetroAchievements Stability
- **No more false bug reports** — When RetroAchievements serves an HTML challenge, rate-limit or maintenance page instead of JSON, both apps now log the condition at Information level and show the normal "no data" state. Previously the JSON parse error was reported as an application bug (bugs #68823–#68828).
- **All RA endpoints covered** — Profile, recently played, completion progress, game details, ranks, earned achievements and session login share the same defensive response handling.

## Updater Fix
- **Read-only files no longer abort the update** — The updater bootstrap clears the read-only attribute before overwriting files such as `LICENSE.txt` (bug #68830). Access-denied and file-in-use conditions are logged at Information and shown with actionable guidance instead of being filed as bugs.

## Dependencies & Maintenance
- **Dependency updates** — Meziantou.Analyzer 3.0.315 and SharpCompress 0.50.7.
- **Packaging** — Windows and Linux bundles are rebuilt as 5.8.4 with the same framework-dependent single-file layout and bundled `LICENSE.txt`, `README.md` and `WhatsNew.md`.

---

steam_rom_manager.releaseNotes:
## Added
- Ability to set overlay images within SRM (only using local images for now). Thanks @Marocco2 for the initial PR.
- Abillty to set sort as title in steam using a custom variable. Thanks @FranKaneStein-g for the initial PR.
-  Arm64 build targets on all three platforms. Thanks @matheus-apolonio for the idea.
- Two new title variables; `${shortcutTitle}` and `${customVariableTitle}`
- Fully deterministic and explicit title waterfall. Each title stage involves at most one change (unlike before, where extracted title was modified several times and didn't necessarily match the title extracted from the parser).
  - extracted title (title produced by the parser)
  - shortcut passthrough title (will only differ if file is a shortcut and shortcut passthrough is enabled)
  - custom variable title (title after applying custom variables)
  - fuzzy title (title after fuzzy match)
  - post title modifier title (title after title modifier field is applied)
  - final title (title after exceptions are applied).

## Fixed
- Two buggy Pokemon Mini presets

stella_android.releaseNotes:
A new major release of Stella is now available; first time in over two years!  Here are some of the changes:

  * Enhanced ROM launcher to allow multiple images per ROM.

  * Made heaps of additional images available for the ROM launcher.

  * Added searching by filename for ROM launcher images.

  * Added option to start random ROM.

  * Added automatically enabled phosphor modes.

  * Enhanced Game Properties dialog for multigame ROMs.

  * Added 2nd UI theme and hotkey for toggling UI theme.

  * Added bezel support (incl. Sinden Lightgun).

  * Added optional type format detection based on colors used.

  * Added Joy2B+ controller support.

  * Added auto detection for QuadTari attached controllers.

  * Enhanced Kid Vid support to play tape audio.

  * Added port selection, used for controller default mapping.

  * Added missing PlusROM support for E7 bankswitching.

  * Enhanced movie cart (MVC) support.

  * Accelerated emulation up to ~15% (ARM).

  * Added limited GameLine Master Module bankswitching support.

  * Added 03E0 bankswitching for Brazilian Parker Bros ROMs.

  * Added WF8 bankswitching used by some certain Coleco white carts.

  * Added JANE bankswitching used by Coleco's Tarzan prototype.

  * Added ELF mapper for Mattress Monkeys.

  * Added BUS bankswitching support for some older demos.

  * Fixed broken 7800 pause key support.

  * Added developer option for random hotspot peek values.

  * Added user defined CPU cycle timers to debugger.

  * Removed 'launcherroms' option, since it was causing some issues.

  * Codebase now uses C++20 features, which means a minimum of gcc-11
    or clang-10 for Linux/Mac, and Visual Studio 2022 for Windows.

-Have fun!

swiff.releaseNotes:
# Version 1.4.1
A smaller update for 1.4.0, just to fix some urgent issues.

## Features
- Added support for x86_64 and ARM32 devices
- Web games can now load embedded Flash, Shockwave and Unity content with Swiff runtimes
- Added an "Allow network connections" option
- Runtimes and support packs are now hosted on Swiff's infrastructure (no more download errors!)
- Shockwave players can now be managed and deleted from Data management

## Fixes
- Improved mouse handling on Wine runtimes for games that lock or hide the cursor (Ex. first-person games)
- Flashpoint Navigator is more stable on ARM devices and waits longer for slow games to start
- Gamepads that report the D-Pad as a hat axis are now detected correctly in the layout editor
- J2ME games that are missing their application file are downloaded again when you launch them
- Fixed Shockwave player installation checks and cleanup
- The runtime update status no longer disappears when refreshing the runtime info
- Checksum errors now show the expected and received hash

Special message, thanks for all the support that you guys gave to Swiff, hopefully the next update will blow your mind!

# X360 Mobile 0.6.3 and X360 Companion 0.1.0

X360 Mobile 0.6.3 introduces local wireless multiplayer through the new X360
Companion application, alongside Android Home shortcuts, a clearer driver
catalog and a unified touch-control system.

## X360 Companion 0.1.0

- Added X360 Companion, a separate Android application that turns a phone on
  the same local network or a paired Bluetooth device into a remote XInput
  controller.
- Up to three companions can be assigned independently to P2, P3 or P4. P1
  remains protected from remote assignment unless the host explicitly enables
  remote-only play.
- Added user-confirmed pairing, trusted-host management, connection recovery,
  per-player rumble and GamerProfile selection on the host.
- Added a shared, localized touch-control editor with compatible TOML
  import/export, presets, Xbox player indicator and controller artwork.
- LAN gameplay was validated between Odin3 and Honor through Gears of War 2.
  Bluetooth remains experimental and device-dependent.

## Library, shortcuts and input

- Added per-game Android Home shortcuts. A shortcut uses a title image embedded
  in supported game content when available, opens the direct-game loading
  screen, applies the game's saved settings and returns to the launcher when
  the game exits.
- Unified the host and Companion touch artwork, layout model and edge-aware
  factory placement. Standard layouts now preserve intended controls that
  extend partially beyond a screen edge on every supported aspect ratio.
- Expanded the integrated driver catalog with release descriptions so users can
  review maintainer compatibility notes before downloading a driver.

## Packages

- **X360 Mobile:** `emu.x360mobile.com`, version `0.6.3` (`versionCode 6039000`),
  asset `x360-mobile-0.6.3.apk`.
- **X360 Companion:** `emu.x360mobile.controller`, version `0.1.0`
  (`versionCode 11002`), asset `x360-companion-0.1.0.apk`.

Both APKs are signed with the established X360 Mobile Release identity. The
emulator uses APK Signature Scheme v3 with a local v4 sidecar; the Companion
also includes v2 for Android 8-12 compatibility.

X360 Mobile remains experimental software. It is not affiliated with Microsoft
or Xbox and must be used only with games and content the user legally owns.

# Xenra 0.4.0

[![Patreon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Patreon-Support_on_Patreon-FF424D?style=for-the-badge&logo=patreon)](https://www.patreon.com/cw/Xanite/membership)

**Xenra 0.4.0** brings a main-thread responsiveness pass, custom Vulkan driver support for Exynos (Mali) devices, experimental temporal frame generation, FATX save streaming, and the consolidation of Xenra into a single free build.

---

## Upgrade Notice

* **Install Direct:** Install Xenra 0.4.0 directly over your existing Green installation. Do not uninstall first, or your configurations, profiles, and shader caches will be deleted.
* **Gold Edition Discontinued:** Gold is retired as of 0.4.0. Installing Green (`Ali.Xanite.green`) will install alongside Gold. Gold data remains intact on your device, but a one-time setup (selecting BIOS, game paths, and granting storage permissions) is required on Green.

---

## Highlights

### Interface & Responsiveness
* **Touch & D-Pad Navigation:** Touch target resolution defers to `ACTION_UP` without walking full view trees. D-pad navigation eliminates ~170 filesystem probes per press for instant library scrolling.
* **Background Log Parsing:** `xe.log` parsing, crash log checks, and tombstone reads moved completely off the main thread across Library and Settings screens.
* **Game Data & HUD:** Directory walks for save folders and CPU/thermal reads for the performance HUD sample on dedicated background lanes without UI stutter.
* **Zero-Allocation Animations:** Glow view animators use quantized, lifecycle-bound cached gradients, eliminating continuous vsync memory allocations.
* **Cold Start Optimization:** IPC permission round-trips collapsed from 5 down to 1, and `/proc/self/maps` parsing moved to a background thread.

### Core Fixes & Memory
* **FATX Save Import Streaming:** Save imports stream in 1 MiB chunks instead of allocating full RAM. Files exceeding the 4 GiB FATX limit are cleanly rejected prior to transfer.
* **JIT Lock & Leak Fix:** Flash writes during hint cache auto-saves no longer hold `mmap_lock` (eliminating mid-game micro-stalls), and a ~3 MB session memory leak was resolved.
* **Boot & Lifecycle Guarding:** Synchronized texture adoption inside render locks to stop black/wrong frame flashes on boot, and prevented double-loads on orientation change.
* **Clean Exits:** Suppressed benign SDL thread teardown alerts on application exit, eliminating phantom "Xenra crashed" toasts.

### Custom GPU Drivers & Frame Generation
* **Exynos (Mali) Support:** Custom Vulkan driver loading is no longer gated by Qualcomm KGSL checks (`/dev/kgsl-3d0`). Mali devices (`/dev/mali`) can now load community driver ZIPs and per-game overrides.
* **Temporal Motion Prediction:** Added an experimental motion vector prediction mode (default off) to stabilize frame generation during fast pans and flat terrain. Toggle live via ADB without restarting:
  `adb shell setprop debug.xanite.fg_temporal_pred 1` (1 = On, 0 = Off)
* **Driver Card UI:** Simplified the GPU driver card to display active runtime driver status without running log parsing operations.

### Netplay & UI Polish
* **Netplay Transport Bootstrap:** Fixed HTTPS transport initialization to bootstrap automatically at boot rather than requiring the diagnostic screen.
* **Cleaned Xbox OG Context Menu:** Context menus for Original Xbox games display only relevant options (`Set Game Folder`), hiding Xbox 360-specific storage entries.

---

## Build Details

Signed with the official Xenra release key (`527f6eb59054f9b0a4f8c661f9b78a9fe80cf4a9ffaff43e0a3727b16226446f`).

| Package Name | Build APK | Version Code |
| :--- | :--- | :---: |
| `Ali.Xanite.green` | `Xenra-0.4.0-green-release.apk` | `31` |
